<!--This is just a template - feel free to delete any and all of it and replace as appropriate.-->

### Description

I just reactivated my PC after lunch, and an active debug-session was in break-mode at this exception:
```
Attempted to divide by zero.
```

StackTrace only contains this method
```
at System.Diagnostics.Tracing.RuntimeEventSourceHelper.GetCpuUsage()
```

Looking at the code it seems like this lines cause the divide by zero:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/57bfe474518ab5b7cfe6bf7424a79ce3af9d6657/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Diagnostics/Tracing/RuntimeEventSourceHelper.Windows.cs#L35-L37

I think (not sure) I reactivated my PC from standby, so this could be a very special case, where  for a brief `totalSystemTime` moment in time is `0`.

review_comments: should make this condition `> 0` instead? just in case run into overflow?

If GetSystemTimes or GetProcessTimes is giving us negative numbers (which I hope never happens) I think it would be beneficial for the cpuUsage value to be obviously bad rather than setting it to a benign looking value like zero.
